title: Reddit's Data Licensing Revenue Grew 24% to $43 Million, With OpenAI and Google as Its Two Biggest Buyers. Here's Why That Number Is So Tiny.
author: John Ballard
description: Reddit's data licensing revenue reached $43 million in Q2 2026, growing 24% year-over-year, but represents only 5% of total revenue. Google and OpenAI are the primary customers using Reddit's data to train AI models. However, advertising remains Reddit's core business and primary growth driver, with the company focusing on converting weekly active users to daily active users to increase ad impressions.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Reddit achieved 8 consecutive quarters of 60%+ revenue growth, with ad revenue climbing 64% YoY to $762 million. Weekly active users grew 24% YoY to 514 million. Data licensing, while small, represents an emerging revenue stream with major tech partners.

Google is noted as Reddit's other major data-licensing customer for AI training purposes. The relationship is presented as transactional and potentially unstable, with no indication of strategic importance to Google's overall business.

title: History Says a $10,000 Investment in the QQQ Will Be Worth $66,000 in 10 Years
author: Neil Patel
description: The Invesco QQQ Trust ETF generated a 563% total return over the past decade, translating to a 20.8% annualized return. If this performance repeats, a $10,000 investment could grow to $66,000 in 10 years. The bull case depends on AI delivering on its promise and generating adequate returns on massive capital expenditures, while the bear case warns of decelerating growth and uncertain AI economic benefits.

description: Major tech companies (Google, Amazon, Meta) are significantly increasing AI infrastructure spending, which benefits not just chip makers like Nvidia, but also less obvious beneficiaries in power generation and uranium supply.
